name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 22, 2015

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Pro Tem Raths at 5:01 p.m., on September 22, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo,
California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 17, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ury
  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Sachs (departed at 6:56 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht (arrived at 5:02 p.m.)

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Initiation of Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (4)
  of Subdivision (d) of Government Code Section 54956.9 (1 case.)

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Raths recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  September 22, 2015
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council gave direction to staff but no reportable
action occurred in Closed Session.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ury

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Schlicht presented a certificate of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter" Lance
  Corporal Cory E. Chavez. Sergeant Major Chamberlin accepted the certificate of
  commendation on behalf of "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant Andrew
  W. McCann who was unable to attend the meeting.

P2.  Recognize Ball Park Pizza Team and High Park Tap House as "Certified Green
  Businesses"

  Mayor Schlicht presented certificates of recognition to John and Valorie Green, owners of
  High Park Tap house and Jim Poettgen, owner of BallPark Pizza.

P4.  Proclaim October 4 through October 10, 2015 To Be Fire Prevention Week

  Mayor Schlicht presented the proclamation to OCFA Battalion Chief Ric Schultz.

P3.  Presentation on "Commerce for a Cause"

  The City Council received the presentation from Scott Carter, Vice President of
  Sports1Marketing.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Stephen Bullard, Laguna Hills: offered Mission Viejo residents a free seminar on solar education
and financing green technology.

Mark Martinez, M.V.: announced that in the month of October, PKSA Karate Studio will host an
eight-week father/daughter self-defense class and he is hosting a five-week financial literacy
class. Additional information is available at www.pksamissionviejo.com and yeseniasdream.org.

City Council Minutes  2  September 22, 2015
 Veronica Stephens, Ladera Ranch: invited residents to an informational presentation on human
trafficking in Orange County. The event will take place on September 28, 2015, at the Murray
Community Center from 7:00 to 9:00 p.m.

Chris Nelson, M.V.: offered city employees chiropractic care insurance through the Good Circle
Insurance Company.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 5, 9, 13, 14, 15, 19, 20, and 21 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate
consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to approve the Consent
Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of September 8, 2015, as
  presented.

4.  Check Register Dated September 4, 2015 in the Amount of $3,104,226.58

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2015

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2015

City Council Minutes  3  September 22, 2015
   Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for July 2015

  Received and filed.

10.  Amendment to Agreement for Oversight Board Legal Services (Harper & Burns
  LLP)

  Approved Amendment to Agreement for Oversight Board Legal Services with Harper &
  Burns LLP in an amount not to exceed $5,000 for each six-month Recognized Obligation
  Payment Schedule (ROPS) period.

11.  Amendment to Agreement For Consultant Services (Arbitrage Compliance
  Specialists)

  Approved Amendment to Agreement for Consultant Services (Arbitrage Compliance
  Specialists, Inc.) for Arbitrage Compliance services in an amount not to exceed $2,100 for
  services related to the Mission Viejo Community Development Finance Authority Variable
  Rate Demand Revenue Bonds (Mission Viejo Mall Improvement Project) 1999 Series A
  for the period of July 1, 2015 - June 30, 2016 as set forth in the Amendment.

12.  Community Development Financing Authority (CDFA) Treasurer’s Annual Report
  for Fiscal Year 2014-15 and Annual Review of the CDFA Investment Policy

  (1) Received and filed the accompanying Treasurer's Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2014-
  15; and (2) adopted CDFA Resolution 15-02 Approving the Authority's Investment Policy
  for FY2015-16.

16.  Revisions to City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Adopted Resolution 15-44 Providing for the Revisions to select Personnel Policies.

17.  Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Renewal

  Approved first amendment to agreement with Digital Map Products; and approve issuance
  of purchase order to Digital Map Products for 2015-16 services in the amount of
  $42,419.00.

18.  2016 Orange County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo

City Council Minutes  4  September 22, 2015
   Approved the request submitted by Pelican Coast Events, LLC to hold the 2016 Orange
  County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo on Sunday, June 5, 2016.

STAFF REPORTS

30.  Mission Viejo Police Services First and Second Quarter Crime Statistics Report

  Lt. Brad NewMyer presented the 2015 first and second quarter Crime Statistics Report and
  answered the City Council Members' questions. Captain Brian Schmutz was also present
  and responded to Council Member comments and questions.

*Note: Council Member Sachs left the meeting at 6:56 p.m. and did not return

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated August 28, 2015 in the Amount of $899,540.29

  Mayor Schlicht asked about restroom rentals for the Animal Shelter ADA restroom project.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that staff
  rented portable restrooms for use during the animal shelter restroom renovation project.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2015

  Mayor Schlicht inquired about an account analysis charge of $25,000.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas responded that the charge is a one-time
  annual fee for banking services.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to receive and
  file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  5  September 22, 2015
   AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2014-15
  and Annual Review of the Mission Viejo Investment Policy

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Mayor Schlicht asked why staff is recommending deleting section D.3.a from the
  Investment Policy and what would stop the immediate sale of a security with a downgrade.

  Director Dyas noted that the policy allows for staff discretion in determining whether to
  sell or hold the security.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, (1) receive and file
  the accompanying Treasurer's Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2014-15; and (2) adopt
  Housing Authority Resolution 15-02 Approving the Mission Viejo Housing Authority
  Investment Policy for FY2015-16.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs

13.  Successor Agency Administrative Budget for the 15-16B Six-Month Fiscal Period of
  January 1, 2016 to June, 30, 2016

  Mayor Schlicht expressed concerned that budget is always about $125,000 and she doesn't
  want to provide opportunity for consultants to create work.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to adopt Successor
  Agency Resolution No. 15-03 Approving the Successor Agency’s Administrative Budget
  for the 15-16B Six-Month Fiscal Period of January 1, 2016 to June 30, 2016 Pursuant to
  Section 34177(j) of the Dissolution Law

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs

City Council Minutes  6  September 22, 2015
 14.  City Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2014-2015 and Annual Review of
  City’s Investment Policy

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Mayor Schlicht stated that she is uncomfortable with the addition of Supranational
  investments and the proposed five-year term.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, (1)
  receive and file the accompanying City Treasurer’s Annual Report for fiscal year 2014-15;
  (2) set the Benchmark Index for FY 2015-16 to be a Government Securities Index
  comprised of 60% three-month Treasury Bills; 25% Treasury and Agency securities with
  maturities greater than one year and up to three years; and 15% Treasury and Agency
  securities with maturities greater than three years and up to five years; (3) update the
  nomenclature of credit agencies and revise throughout the policy as necessary; and (4)
  delete section D.4.a from the investment policy.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to amend
  the investment policy to add high quality, highly rated California municipal securities and
  securities issued by specific Supranational organizations to the list of permitted
  investments.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  Sachs

15.  Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the 15-16B Six-Month Fiscal Period of
  January 1, 2016 to June 30, 2016

  Mayor Schlicht stated that she is uncomfortable that the report was released to the Council
  at the same time that it was released to the Successor Agency Board.

  Director of Administrative Services Dyas announced that she notified the Board Members
  that she would provide an update should the Council make any changes tonight.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to adopt
  Successor Agency Resolution 15-04 Approving the Recognized Obligation Payment

City Council Minutes  7  September 22, 2015
   Schedule for the 15-16B Six-Month Fiscal Period of January 1, 2016 to June 30, 2016,
  Subject to Submittal to and Review by the Oversight Board and the Department of Finance
  Pursuant to California Health and Safety Code, Division 24, Part 1.85, as amended by
  Assembly Bill 1484.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs

19.  Bocce Ball Courts at the Oso Viejo Community Park - (CIP 324)

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the report.

  Anna T. Boyce, M.V.: asked the Council to approve the Community Services Commission
  recommendation to move forward with the bocce ball courts.

  Diane Weston, M.V.: asked the Council to approve the bocce ball courts at Oso Viejo
  Community Park.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  approve the plans and specifications and authorized staff to advertise for bids for the Bocce
  Ball Courts at the Oso Viejo Community Park – (CIP 324).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs

20.  Recreational Trails Program Grant Application-Arroyo Trabuco Regional Multi-Use
  Trail Access and Regional Connector

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Mayor Schlicht asked if this matter was ever discussed at a Community Services
  Commission (CSC) meeting.

  Director Chagnon responded that the proposed trail connection had been discussed by the
  CSC. He also noted that another grant application for the same project was submitted last
  June under the federal Active Transportation Program (ATP) and that the Recreational
  Trails Program (RTP) application would be a back-up should the ATP application be
  unsuccessful.

City Council Minutes  8  September 22, 2015
   Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to adopt
  Resolution 15-45 Approving the Application for Grant Funds from the Recreational Trails
  Program.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  Sachs

21.  Trabuco Road & Marguerite Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation Project, CIP 837

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Mayor Schlicht read an email question that she sent to Director Chagnon and his
  response. She expressed concern with the process for professional services proposals. She
  stated that all the consultants were pre-qualified and therefore she doesn't know how they
  were given different grades.

  Director Chagnon noted that the City engineers estimate what the design costs will be and
  this consultant's price was right in line with that estimate.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Schlicht, to authorize issuance
  of a purchase order for design services for the subject project to Joseph C. Truxaw and
  Associates, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $69,950.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs

NEW BUSINESS

22.  Ordinance Adding Chapter 8.14 to the Municipal Code, to Provide an Expedited,
  Streamlined Permitting Process for Small Residential Rooftop Solar Systems

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to adopt
  Urgency Ordinance 15-305 Amending Mission Viejo Municipal Code, Title 8, Building
  and Construction by Adding Chapter 8.14 Relating to the Permitting Process for Small
  Residential Rooftop Solar Systems.

City Council Minutes  9  September 22, 2015
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to introduce
  Ordinance 15-306 Amending Mission Viejo Municipal Code, Title 8, Building and
  Construction by Adding Chapter 8.14, Relating To The Permitting Process For Small
  Residential Rooftop Solar Systems.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs

23.  Various Speed Limit Updates

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Mayor Schlicht asked if the data was collected by the number of cars or within a specified
  time frame.

  Director Chagnon responded that he would have to get back to the Council with an answer
  to that question.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to introduce
  Ordinance 15-307 Amending Chapter 12.04.010(d) of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code
  Regarding Prima Facie Speed Limits on Certain Streets.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed his continued concern with various issues at the Orange
County Fire Authority.

24.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

City Council Minutes  10  September 22, 2015
   Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that he had nothing to report.

25.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  There was no report due to Council Member Sachs' absence.

26.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

27.  Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) Programs Ad Hoc Committee

  Mayor Schlicht appointed herself and Council Member Bucknum to the ad hoc committee.

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

28.  Recommended Names for the Wall of Recognition Display

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented report.

  Sharon Cody, M.V.: stated that Sherri Butterfield should be included on the Wall of
  Recognition for her tireless efforts to see that her dream of a Mission Viejo Library came
  to fruition.

  Mayor Schlicht stated that she is not supportive of adding Mrs. Butterfield's name because
  she does not think it is s right for elected officials to be included on the Wall of Recognition.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to
  approve the recommended names for the Initial Wall of Recognition Display, including
  Sherri Butterfield, and to put a policy in place that elected officials are not precluded from
  the Wall of Recognition.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Ury, to call
  the question.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  Sachs

  On roll call, said MAIN motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  11  September 22, 2015
   AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  Sachs

  Mayor Schlicht stated that it was her desire to bifurcate the motion. Her vote against Mrs.
  Butterfield was not political but instead was her support for the Community Services
  Commission's recommendation that former elected officials should not be part of the Wall
  of Recognition.

RECESS

At the hour of 7:59 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:10
p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Sachs was absent.)

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

29.  El Nino 2015-2016 Weather Event Report

  Emergency Services Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report and Assistant
  City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay answered the Council Members
  questions.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

31.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

 Council Member Bucknum

 Council Member Bucknum discussed her attendance at an open house at the South Orange
 County Veterans Center which assists veterans who were significantly injured in the line of
 duty. She also attended a very respectful ceremony for Patriots Day hosted by City staff and
 anyone who wanted to participate. She noted that in past, local Boy Scout Troops organized
 events on 9/11 and she hopes that staff will work with the local groups so there can be a nice
 public event for Patriots Day next year. Council Member Bucknum also discussed her
 attendance at the 17th annual business expo at the Norman P. Murray Community Center. It was
 a great showcase for businesses and restaurants and was very well attended as it is every
 year. She also attended the Inner Coastal Cleanup of Oso Creek and she noted that kids had fun
 cleaning up and getting muddy and it was nice to see the Nadadores and all the scout and church
 groups participating. Council Member Bucknum highlighted the annual shred event at Mission
 Viejo High School and the Mission for the Armed Forces football game. She congratulated
City Council Minutes  12  September 22, 2015
  High Park Tap House and Ballpark Pizza for becoming the City’s first two green businesses.
 Both have been in business in the community for many years and they have been very supportive
 of the City and youth sports teams. Council Member Bucknum reminded residents of the OCFA
 message “Hear the Beep Where You Sleep” and encouraged everyone to make sure their safety
 alarms are up to date and batteries have been changed. She expressed thanks to the City Clerk
 for the nice photographs and story in the Outlook publication on the Marguerite Aquatics
 complex renovation. She also thanked Mayor Pro Tem Raths for working with Action Force
 Network on the September 28 event that will inform the community about human trafficking
 and the dangers teenagers face. Lastly, Council Member Bucknum thanked Mayor Schlicht for
 allowing her to serve on the PACE Programs ad hoc committee and she stated that she looks
 forward to creating beneficial information for residents.

 Council Member Sachs

 Council Member Ury

 Mayor Pro Tem Raths

 Mayor Pro Tem Raths acknowledged that he has been on the City Council for ten months and
 he has really enjoyed it. He noted that he has gotten to know the staff and worked closely with
 them; if he has questions on anything, staff has been very responsive and he expressed his
 appreciation for that. Mayor Pro Tem Raths noted that the Mayor pulled nine Consent Calendar
 items this evening and he reminded her that staff is there to provide help so there are no “gotcha”
 questions. He discussed resident Larry Gilbert’s comments at the last Council meeting and
 stated that it is a tit for tat type of thing. He said that he is on the Council to serve the community
 and there is no other motive. He volunteers and helps many organizations and he stated that he
 uses his position as Mayor Pro Tem to help these organizations and that’s it. Mayor Pro Tem
 Raths stated that he will continue to call Mr. Gilbert out when he questions his integrity and
 moral character. Referring to the cover story on the new issue of Outlook magazine, he thanked
 the City Clerk and stated that he is excited for the renovation of the aquatics center. He also
 referenced the Outlook article on the Rotary Club and announced that he will be in charge of the
 Texas Hold ‘Em tournament next year on June 11, 2016. Finally, Mayor Pro Tem Raths
 announced that Assemblyman Bill Brough will host a Veterans Fair on October 3, 2015,
 beginning at 11:00 a.m. at Capistrano Valley High School.

 Mayor Schlicht

 Mayor Schlicht thanked Lance Corporal Chavez and Sergeant Major Chamberlin for their
 service to our country and for choosing something greater than themselves. She stated that she
 is proud that the City and its residents do so much to support Headquarters Battalion of the 1st
 Marine Division. Regarding Consent Calendar items, Mayor Schlicht stated that it is not a
 “gotcha.” The public used to have the ability to pull consent calendar items and ask questions
 and they no longer do. She stated that it’s a public meeting and she really doesn’t like doing
 things behind the scenes so she will continue to pull consent calendar items when she has
 questions. Discussing the City’s responses to three Grand Jury reports, she stated that she is fine
 with staff’s letters. Mayor Schlicht mentioned recent complaints about noise coming from the

City Council Minutes  13  September 22, 2015
  soccer field at the YMCA and she referenced a noise report that was done for the Nadadores.
 She said she would give it to the City Clerk for the public record. She asked Mayor Pro Tem
 Raths if he would like to go with her to meet the City’s auditors and she asked the City Attorney
 to provide a public update on the Medical Marijuana Regulation and Safety Act. Discussing a
 proposed bill that threatened to reduce Orange County cities representation on the Orange
 County Fire Authority Board of Directors, Mayor Schlicht noted that some cities had threatened
 to leave OCFA and she wondered if her colleagues would like staff to conduct a study and look
 at Mission Viejo’s options. She further asked the City Attorney to provide the Council with an
 update on a claim against the city by Julie Bronson for an incident at the Nadadores
 facility. Mayor Shclicht announced two upcoming events for veterans, the 2015 Toshiba Classic
 Military Appreciation Day on October 31 and a Veterans Resource Fair on October 3 at
 Capistrano Valley High School. She also outlined her attendance at recent events including the
 Mission Viejo High School armed forces tribute, an inspirational talk by radio host Larry Elder
 on working hard and never giving up, an El Toro Water District Meeting where she raised
 concerns about tiered rates, a Rush Limbaugh meeting with guest speakers from Immunity
 Education Group on the topic of forced vaccinations, and a Casta del Sol Republican Club
 presentation called “Terrorism – A Clear and Present Danger” which encouraged residents to
 report anything suspicious that they see. Mayor Schlicht discussed her time with 4th grade
 students at Carl Hankey School and her attendance at an event at the Balboa Bay Club where
 John Easton of the Claremont Institute Center for Constitutional Jurisprudence was the guest
 speaker. Mr. Easton is a leading scholar on the Constitution and she discussed what she learned
 about the country’s weakening doctrine. She stated that we are supposed to be a nation of laws
 not a nation of men and viewpoints and that’s what we the country has devolved into. Mayor
 Schlicht asked residents to get involved and please contact her if they need more information on
 where to go. She discussed her attendance at a Mission Calvary sermon, handing out awards
 for the annual photography show, and the solemn ceremony on Patriots Day where she became
 interested in Michael Simon who died on 9/11. She Googled him and shared what she had
 learned about his life. In conclusion, Mayor Schlicht read a quote from George Washington:
 “The power under the Constitution will always be in the People. It is entrusted for certain defined
 purposes, and for a certain limited period, to representatives of their own choosing; and
 whenever it is executed contrary to their Interest, or not agreeable to their wishes, their Servants
 can, and undoubtedly will be, recalled.”

 ADJOURNMENT

 At the hour of 8:54 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
 Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, October 13, 2015, at 5:00 p.m.

 ______________________________________________
 Karen Hamman, City Clerk

 Approved at the meeting of October 13, 2015

City Council Minutes  14  September 22, 2015
